title: sync's re-run after a code-changing rebase keeps the merge sides for fix
goal: When kbgit.py sync re-runs itself because its rebase changed kbgit.py (ST-sajrwz6a), the re-run still repairs a source-id or answer-id collision that both sides added: the parent passes the rebase's base, upstream and side to the child (or runs fix with them before re-running), so a union-merged id collision is renumbered as before instead of exiting 3 with 'sides unknown, pass --side'. A test in test_sync.py plants an incoming kbgit.py change plus a colliding source id on both sides. Found by the SP-x2pvljz6 review (F1, kbgit.py sync_once and fix_args).
